text: A flotation is the moment a private company first offers its shares to the public on a stock exchange. Americans usually say IPO. Here it is Anthropic's stock-market debut, which gave its employees' shares a daily price.

Benign means gentle or harmless, the opposite of malignant. The joke word "Anthropalypse" sounds like a disaster, but the article says it is more benign than it sounds: it describes a flood of money for charities.
To be discomfited is to feel uneasy or embarrassed, thrown off balance. The founder felt awkward about a lavish sushi spread that did not suit the company's simple culture.
To toil is to work hard for a long time, often at something tiring. The article says the 5,000-odd people who toil at Anthropic, a slightly grand way of saying they work there.
A windfall is a sudden, unexpected gain of money, like fruit blown off a tree. For charities, the Anthropic shares pledged to them would be a huge windfall.
Tidy usually means neat, but before a sum of money it means large. A tidy $470bn is a joking understatement, since that is an enormous amount.
A stake is a share of ownership in a company. The founders' roughly equal stakes were each a similar-sized slice of Anthropic, and they set aside 80% of those slices for charity.
To set aside something is to keep it apart for a particular purpose. The founders set aside most of their shares for charity from the very start.
A startup is a young company, often built around a new idea and hoping to grow fast. Startup bosses rarely plan charity until their firm is sold or listed.
Market value is the total price investors put on all of a company's shares. The founders' pledges are worth more than Facebook's entire market value when it listed in 2012.
To pledge is to make a serious promise, such as to give money. A pledge is not yet a payment, so the money may take years to arrive.
In a matching scheme an employer adds money to what staff give, often dollar for dollar. It tops up the employees' own pledges and adds almost another $100bn.
"Ants" is a nickname the article uses for Anthropic's employees, a pun on the company's name. The colony image returns in the last line.
A kitty is a shared pool of money that people pay into for a common purpose. Here it is the fund holding 5% of Anthropic's shares for charity.
This is the charity-oriented fund that Anthropic has promised 5% of its shares to. Public benefit means the aim is to help society, not just earn profit.
The public good means what helps everyone in society rather than one person or company. Anthropic says about 20% of its stock will be dedicated to it.
To materialise is to actually appear or come true, rather than stay a promise. The article says the giving may take years to materialise, or some of it may never.
Here evaporates is used about money: it means to vanish gradually, like water drying up. If the share price falls, pledged gifts could shrink or disappear.
Unprecedented means never having happened before. The article says no one has seen this much money heading toward charities at once.
Ultra Philanthropy is a firm that advises rich donors on where to give. Philanthropy means giving money to improve people's lives.
A joke word blending Anthropic with apocalypse, the end of the world. It is meant playfully: the shock is a flood of giving, not a disaster.
Effective altruists try to do the most good per dollar, using evidence to compare charities. Many work in or near the AI world.
Well-meaning describes someone with good intentions, whatever the results. The article calls effective altruists well-meaning if sometimes overzealous.
Overzealous means too eager, pushing an idea or rule further than is sensible. It is a mild criticism of effective altruists.
To benefit handsomely means to gain a lot. Handsomely here has nothing to do with looks; it means generously or in a big way.
Giving What We Can is a group whose members pledge to donate 10% of their lifetime income to the most effective charities. GWWC is its abbreviation.
These are dangers that could harm huge numbers of people worldwide, such as pandemics or out-of-control AI. Some charities work on preventing them.
Rogue means behaving outside the control of its owners. Rogue AI is the fear of an AI system that pursues its own goals and cannot be stopped.
A trust is a legal arrangement where one person or institution holds money for someone else. The employees set trusts up in the names of parents or siblings.
Spouseless means having no husband or wife. The writer uses it to describe young, single workers who have no household to support.
Student loans are money borrowed to pay for college that must be repaid with interest. Paying them off is a very sensible first use of sudden wealth.
To dive into something is to jump into it eagerly, often without much caution. The writer suggests many may rush into San Francisco's housing market.
Ultra-hot here means extremely competitive, with prices rising fast and buyers fighting over homes. It is a market term, not a temperature.
A mansion shortage is a joke: so many newly rich people want huge houses that big homes are running out.
Conventional displays of wealth are the usual ways of showing off, like yachts, fancy cars and luxury meals. The article says these are unlikely to appeal to Ants.
Tbh is internet shorthand for to be honest. The founder's casual Slack message shows how informal and modest the early culture was.
Science-fictional means like something from a sci-fi story. Ants dream of rocket cars and robot exoskeletons, not gold watches.
An exoskeleton is a hard frame worn outside the body. A robotic one would move with the wearer and help them lift or walk, which Mr Clark imagined for his back spasms.
To diversify investments is to spread money across many different things so one failure cannot ruin you. It is sensible when nearly all your wealth is one company's stock.
PitchBook is a company that collects data on startups and investment deals. Its analyst expects some of the money to flow into new startups.
To bloom is to flower and thrive. The closing line plays on the ant colony image, hoping both new companies and charities grow.
